phase_name: Permission Broker Production Consumption Contract Freeze
summary: Froze PBPC-001 v1.0, the normative contract governing how pcae push must consume the Permission Broker Foundation (POL-001..012, permission_broker_foundation.py) as its mandatory centralized permission-decision boundary. Independently reconstructed the Foundation and current pcae push implementation (src/pcae/commands/push.py) from primary source rather than Phase 148A's summary prose: found two discrepancies (decision vocabulary is three values ALLOW/DENY/HUMAN_REVIEW not four; HARD_BLOCK_REGISTRY has 12 entries not 11 -- both OBSERVATION, non-Blocking), that pcae push has two independent git push dispatch sites (ordinary path and --staged-file-aware path, both now bound by the contract's non-bypassability requirements), and that only POL-001 (missing active task) among existing push readiness conditions maps onto a currently-implemented Foundation policy rule -- a coverage gap documented honestly rather than closed with new policy. The contract resolves Phase 148A's open questions: broker consolidation (Foundation only; legacy permission_broker.py unchanged/undeprecated), the POL-005 misclassification risk (simulation_only=True for all push requests), ownership model, operation identity, non-bypassability, TOCTOU, replay/restart, failure ownership, diagnostics, security threat model, and durable-artifact assessment (Option A selected, no new artifact, audit persistence deferred to 148C). IWC-REQ-029 preserved unmodified (no amendment required); Authority Evaluation/AESIC independence preserved, not reopened. Contract-only phase: no src/pcae/** modification (confirmed via git diff), no runtime-capability change, no existing frozen-contract amendment. No Blocking finding. See docs/PHASE_148B_PERMISSION_BROKER_PRODUCTION_CONSUMPTION_CONTRACT_FREEZE.md and docs/contracts/PERMISSION_BROKER_PRODUCTION_CONSUMPTION_CONTRACT.md for full detail. Verdict: PHASE 148B COMPLETE. PBPC-001 v1.0 FROZEN.
